- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg 0.0–0.1), model overestimates mean → adjust downward by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- Model frequently underestimates early in 30d forecast when sentiment is negative → add 1–3% to first 5–7 days if sentiment < -0.1.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.4 to +0.1 in 3 days), model lags → shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is below 70.00, model often overpredicts → apply 3–5% downward bias if sentiment is weak or flat.
